description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:1493-1505 splits one logical lookup ("find the EKU extension") into two `.ok_or` calls that both produce the same fixed-string error:

```rust
let exts = leaf
    .tbs_certificate
    .extensions
    .as_ref()
    .ok_or(Error::ProfileViolation {
        reason: Cow::Borrowed("TSA certificate has no ExtendedKeyUsage extension"),
    })?;
let ext = exts
    .iter()
    .find(|e| e.extn_id == OID_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE)
    .ok_or(Error::ProfileViolation {
        reason: Cow::Borrowed("TSA certificate has no ExtendedKeyUsage extension"),
    })?;
```

The two failure cases (`extensions == None` and `extensions == Some(empty)`-or-`Some(no-EKU)`) produce byte-identical error messages, which is the correct behaviour — the caller cannot distinguish them. But the source has the same error literal in two places.

The same module already has the idiomatic one-liner at `aia_extract.rs:67-75`:

```rust
fn find_extension_value<'a>(cert: &'a Certificate, oid: &ObjectIdentifier) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    cert.tbs_certificate
        .extensions
        .as_deref()
        .unwrap_or(&[])
        .iter()
        .find(|e| &e.extn_id == oid)
        .map(|e| e.extn_value.as_bytes())
}
```

Adopted here:

```rust
let ext = leaf
    .tbs_certificate
    .extensions
    .as_deref()
    .unwrap_or(&[])
    .iter()
    .find(|e| e.extn_id == OID_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE)
    .ok_or(Error::ProfileViolation {
        reason: Cow::Borrowed("TSA certificate has no ExtendedKeyUsage extension"),
    })?;
```

One `.ok_or`, one error literal, no possibility of the two literals drifting apart in a future refactor (e.g. someone tweaks one wording but not the other, producing inconsistent error output depending on which path was taken).

What goes wrong if it stays: two identical string literals are bug bait. A typo-fix or wording change applied to one but not the other becomes a silent inconsistency — the same logical failure produces different error strings depending on which branch happened to execute. The `.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])` pattern is already established in this file at `aia_extract.rs` — consistency favours using it here too.
title: enforce_timestamping_eku_critical_and_sole: two .ok_or with identical error strings; use .as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])
